name: Siege of Veii
intro: Veii, the great Etruscan city twelve miles north of Rome, about 396 BC. The war has lasted years, and Roman tradition makes the siege last ten, like Troy. You command the besieging army, which will become Camillus’s.
debrief: In Livy’s account, Rome began paying its soldiers so they could keep up the siege through the winters. Capena and Falerii tried to relieve Veii and were beaten off. The dictator Marcus Furius Camillus had a tunnel dug through the soft rock into the citadel, under the temple of Juno, and while the army attacked the walls, picked men came up through it and opened the city. Veii fell and its land became Roman. The details, especially the ten years, are coloured by legend, but the fall of Veii was real and doubled Rome’s territory. The other choices are what-ifs.

win: Roman soldiers rise into the temple of Juno.
lose: The siege drags on another year.
Veii still stands across the Tiber.

decisions.title: Ten years
decisions.text: Rome has besieged Veii, the great Etruscan city across the Tiber, for years. The army has had to stay in the field through the winter, and it needs pay.

hint.text: Men who must serve all year need to be paid.

scout.text: Pay the soldiers from the treasury so they can stay at the siege through winter.

choices.label: Pay the army so it can stay all winter

fx.text: For the first time, Roman soldiers are paid. The siege lines stay manned through the winter.

choices.label: Send the men home each winter as usual

fx.text: Each spring the siege starts again.

choices.label: Storm the walls now and end it

fx.text: The walls are too strong; the attack fails.

decisions.title: Allies to the rescue
decisions.text: The neighbouring towns of Capena and Falerii march to help Veii and attack your lines from outside.

hint.text: The relief comes from the north.

scout.text: Turn part of the army to face them while the siege lines hold.

choices.label: Turn part of the army to meet them

fx.text: Part of the army turns and drives off the Capenates and Faliscans.

choices.label: Hold the siege lines and ignore them
Give up the siege and fight them in the field

fx.text: Veii is supplied while you are away.

decisions.title: A new dictator
decisions.text: The siege has dragged on under quarrelling commanders. Marcus Furius Camillus is named dictator.

hint.text: The hill under Veii is soft rock.

scout.text: A tunnel under the walls would open a way into the city itself.

choices.label: Dig a tunnel under the walls into the city

fx.text: Six shifts dig day and night through the soft rock toward the citadel.

choices.label: Build a siege mound against the walls

fx.text: The mound grows slowly under Veientine missiles.

choices.label: Assault the walls in many places at once

decisions.title: The tunnel is ready
decisions.text: The tunnel has reached the citadel, under the temple of Juno. The defenders know nothing.

hint.text: The defenders must be kept busy on the walls.

scout.text: Attack the walls everywhere at once, so no one looks to the citadel, then break out of the tunnel.

choices.label: Attack the walls to draw them, then open the tunnel

fx.text: While the Veientines rush to the walls, picked men burst up into the temple of Juno, open the gates and let the army in.

choices.label: Send the tunnellers in alone at night

fx.text: The small party is found and fights its way to a gate.

choices.label: Wait for them to starve instead: they cannot hold out for ever

decisions.title: Veii falls
decisions.text: Roman soldiers are inside the walls. The city is falling.

hint.text: The Veientines are still fighting in the streets.

scout.text: Promise mercy to those who lay down their arms, so the fighting ends quickly.

choices.label: Spare anyone who lays down his arms

fx.text: Camillus has it announced that the unarmed will be spared. The fighting stops; the city is Rome’s.

choices.label: Let the soldiers sack the city at will

fx.text: The sack is savage and the fighting drags on in the streets.

choices.label: Pull back and make them surrender formally

fx.text: The defenders rally on the walls.
